features.label: Chat
features.scope: Chat entrypoint and TUI are present in the public tree as the daily interaction mode.
limitations: Ordinary coding-loop reliability is under active qualification.
Provider-backed sessions require local credentials and a working provider; quality varies by model.

features.label: Plan
features.scope: Plan mode exists as a CLI/TUI entrypoint for planning before mutation.
limitations: Planning behavior boundaries are documented in the product source.
No live workflow qualification is claimed.

features.label: Deep
features.scope: Deep mode exists as a higher-ceremony path intended for riskier work.
limitations: Still maturing; route availability is not a reliability ranking.
Deep is not a blanket reliability upgrade over Chat.

features.label: Doctor environment checks
features.scope: babel doctor reports environment prerequisites (runtime, providers, Docker).
limitations: Output is diagnostic; a clean doctor report is not a coding-reliability score.

features.label: Desktop shell
features.scope: Electron Desktop shell and a Windows x64 portable preview are published through the v0.1.1 GitHub release; the opening screen is an explicitly labeled reference preview.
limitations: The published Windows portable preview is unsigned; SmartScreen may warn.
Installer lifecycle (install/upgrade/rollback/uninstall), code signing, and automatic updates are not part of the published distribution.
Active model-task shutdown on quit and cross-version profile migration are unqualified.

features.label: Execution profiles
features.scope: Profile policy (safe_repo default with Docker isolation, dev_local, and others) is implemented and covered by enforcement tests.
limitations: The default safe_repo profile fail-closes without Docker.
dev_local permits intrinsic inspection commands only; project-code tests/builds are denied without isolation.

features.label: MCP read-only inspection
features.scope: A read-only MCP inspection entrypoint exists for control-plane style inspection.
limitations: Inspection surface only; not a general execution API.

features.label: Ordinary coding-loop reliability
features.scope: Everyday repository work reliability is explicitly under active qualification upstream.
limitations: No general reliability claim is made or implied anywhere on this site.
Scoped test passes are not a live-model quality score.

distributions.label: npm registry package (babel-harness)
distributions.reason: No package is published to the npm registry. The v0.1.1 release attaches an npm-format tarball (babel-harness-0.1.1.tgz) on GitHub for transparency, but publishing to the registry is a separate owner-authorized flow and no install command for that tarball is documented. The supported install path is clone + build.

distributions.label: Windows x64 portable preview (Desktop shell + CLI)
Windows Setup.exe installer
distributions.reason: No Setup.exe is attached to v0.1.1. Installer lifecycle qualification exists only as CI work; the published Desktop artifact is the unsigned portable ZIP.

distributions.label: GitHub release v0.1.0
distributions.reason: Release v0.1.0 (2026-07-23) is a source tag only — it carries no downloadable assets.

evidence.supports: Source-only install path (clone + build) and its documented commands.
Chat mode entrypoint and documented behavior surface.
Plan mode entrypoint documented in the product start-here guide.
Deep mode entrypoint documented in the product start-here guide.
Doctor command documented with its diagnostic scope.
Desktop shell scope: unsigned Windows portable preview, optional Setup.exe builder, reference-preview opening screen.
Windows preview is unsigned; no code-signing identity, SmartScreen reputation, updater, Start Menu registration, or uninstaller is provided.
Execution profile policy definitions, including dev_local's inspection-only scope.
Upstream status: availability vs qualification separation, MCP inspection entrypoint, active-qualification statement, no published npm package.
Release v0.1.0 exists as a tag with zero published assets (observed via GitHub API).
Release v0.1.1 published 2026-10-07 with a Windows x64 portable ZIP (sha256 disclosed in SHA256SUMS), an npm-format CLI tarball, a file manifest, and SHA256SUMS; the bundle is unsigned.

The tag workflow builds the unsigned Windows portable bundle (it fails unless BUILD.json signed=false), requires exactly one SHA256SUMS entry, and stages the CLI tarball for transparency while stating npm publishing is a separate authorized flow.
npm registry publishing exists only as a separate, owner-authorized workflow added after v0.1.1; it has not produced a published registry package.
